doc.title: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum Interview, 1960-10-16
doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Little George starts on trumpet; Joe Howard
summary: Little George began music at about 14, studied briefly with Joe Howard, and went on his own; Joe Howard was a fine trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: What is it? Well, I'll tell you that. Can you tell us any more about your son, and we didn't talk too much about him? That's his girlfriend. How old was he when he started to play? Do you remember? He can't go far with you, but that's her girlfriend.

Oh, as soon as his dad got his son. Her girlfriend, yes. He started to do music. Yes. And Joe Howard taught him a couple of months, and that was all. I got to graduate in graduate school. I used to teach him before I became a supervisor. He was 14. He wasn't quite 14 when he was daddy. And during that spring, he started to take the music. He didn't study with his father then at all? No, not with his father at all. Uh-uh, not with his father at all. But Joe Howard started. Joe. It was then Joe. Oh, man. You remember Joe? Joe Howard, yeah. Oh, man. And he taught him to sing. But he sang, Mr. McCollum, you let George come, and I won't try to run the thing. George didn't take music a year from Joe. And he went on his own.
